context: Small stdlib-only script under _project/scripts; wire into .pre-commit-config.yaml and/or the Makefile lint aggregate that CI runs. Reject only a revision DECREASE; unchanged and increased revisions pass so legitimate lock updates need no ceremony.
description: Successor of uv-lock-revision-downgrade-guard (dropped 2026-07-31: its single rung was the prose placeholder '<new guard invocation>' - not a runnable command; it fails the shell parse with exit 2 on ANY tree, so it could never distinguish unfixed from fixed, and it is exactly the rung class todo-lint-unrunnable-verification-commands-2 exists to catch). Premise (re-validated 2026-07-31): uv.lock on develop is at `revision = 3`; an older local uv rewrites it to revision 2 as a silent side effect alongside a real dependency change, and nothing rejects that diff. Add a concrete guard: `_project/scripts/check_uv_lock_revision.py`, with a testable interface `--old N --new N` (used by the rung below) and a default mode that compares HEAD:uv.lock against the working tree for pre-commit/CI wiring. The rung fixes the guard's invocation contract at create time so it stays falsifiable: absent script = exit 1 (unmet), present-and-correct = exit 0.

preserves.behavior: Legitimate uv.lock updates still work without special ceremony

verifications.command: f=_project/scripts/check_uv_lock_revision.py; test -f "$f" && ! uv run --project _project/scripts -- python "$f" --old 3 --new 2 && uv run --project _project/scripts -- python "$f" --old 3 --new 3
verifications.description: the guard exists, rejects a 3->2 downgrade, and accepts an unchanged revision
verifications.expected: exits 1 on the unfixed tree (guard script absent = criterion unmet; verified 2026-07-31); exits 0 once the guard exists with the --old/--new test interface and the right accept/reject behavior

verifications.description: guard is wired into a gate that actually runs (pre-commit or the CI make lint aggregate)
verifications.expected: exits 1 on the unfixed tree (verified 2026-07-31: no references exist); exits 0 once wired
